summary: Mobile handover + token rotation suppresses SSE terminal sentence during resume
description: Issue summary: Customer AtlasDocs reports that when their mobile users switch network connectivity (cellular <-> Wi-Fi) during a long-lived SSE chat session, the final sentence from the assistant is sometimes missing after the client reconnects. Impact: Enterprise customer reports multiple support tickets and partial message loss for end users, causing trust issues with summarization and billing disputes. Environment: Production, us-west-2, Dedicated customer cluster for AtlasDocs, sessions originate from mobile webview using Redwood Mobile SDK v1.4.2. Observed behavior: On network handover we see a resume attempt from the client; the gateway accepts the new connection but the terminal SSE event ("[END]"-style closing event / final chunk) is not delivered to the client. Server logs show resume validation warnings tied to a short-lived auth rotation. Expected behavior: After a transient network change the client should resume and receive the remaining final tokens and closing event, preserving sentence boundaries and metadata.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Start a long-running SSE chat session against the hosted API (redwood-v1-medium) from the mobile webview using Mobile SDK v1.4.2.
2) During model generation, toggle network from cellular to Wi-Fi (or enable airplane-mode then re-enable) to force a reconnect/different NAT path.
3) Observe client resume handshake and final assembly of tokens; in affected cases the final sentence/closing paragraph does not arrive and stream remains idle until idle-timeout.
4) Reproduces reliably for AtlanticDocs QA when auth rotation happens within ~10s window of the handover.
Notes: Repro is timing-dependent and more likely on poor cellular networks or when the customer's identity provider rotates short-lived session tokens on refresh.
logs: 2026-03-12T18:03:11.148Z auth[oauth] WARN token_age_exceeded token_id=tok-789 ttl=8s user=atlas-user-42
investigation_notes: Initial triage (Support): reproduced with AtlasDocs test harness while toggling mobile network; pattern correlates with auth refresh that rotates token TTL to very short-lived (<= 10s) values.

SRE trace: resume-handler accepts the TCP/websocket handshake and routes to serving-runtime, but the resume validation logs a 'auth_grace_expired' path which leads to a 'soft-accept' where the connection is allowed but finalization path is not triggered.

Hypothesis: race between client resume and token rotation leads to resume being accepted but the server not emitting terminal/closing marker because the resume provenance check failed final validation. The client never receives the closing marker and therefore the last sentence is missing (stream silently idle until timeout).

Root cause candidate: auth rotation window for token-bound resume checks is shorter than the network handover jitter window, causing the resume path to skip terminal flush. The serving-runtime currently expects an explicit terminal emission from resume reconciler when the previous stream was mid-sentence; that emission is gated on full resume validation.
Cross-reference: See SUP-420420 for other cases of proxy-induced terminal marker loss (network handoffs + edge retries).
mitigation: Short-term workaround for customer: disable aggressive auth TTL rotation on AtlasDocs identity provider for a 60s grace window around session refresh, or pin SDK to use session-based opaque token (instead of per-request rotating token).
Server-side temporary mitigation: enable experimental 'resume-auth-grace' feature flag to increase token age tolerance on resume endpoints to 30s for AtlasDocs dedicated cluster (applied by infra).
Client-side mitigation: update Mobile SDK to buffer and re-request missing terminal event with an explicit 'fetch_missing_tail' call if resume completes without END marker (planned quick patch).
resolution_plan: Short term (24-72h): enable 'resume-auth-grace' flag for AtlasDocs and roll mobile sdk patch that retries terminal fetch. Track customer's incidence rate post-change.

Medium term (2-4 weeks): modify resume-handler to do a two-phase resume: provisional accept + deferred terminal reconciliation that will emit terminal chunk even if auth rotation occurs within grace window. Add server-side audit event for 'terminal_omission' to alert on future regressions.

Long term (quarter): add integration test simulating mobile network handovers and auth rotation timing to CI, and document recommended auth TTL best-practices for mobile clients in the Redwood Private onboarding guide.
Related PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serve/pull/4123 implements provisional accept logic and adds a metrics counter 'resume_terminal_missing_count'.
